{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

In addition, a divine beast mirror and copper bells were excavated. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 2 |{{nihongo|''{{ill|Square Kofun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} square mound |About 40 meters on a side | Surrounding moat exists. More than 100 ''haniwa'' were unearthed in a row on the outer bank. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 3 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} (uncertain) |Diameter about 30 meters | |- |Tsukuriyama No. 4 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound or {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Length 55 meters |Cylindrical and figurative ''haniwa'' (house-shaped and armor-shaped) excavated from the edge of the mound. |- |Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5) |{{nihongo|{{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=''hotategata'' kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}|帆立貝形古墳||}} scallop-shaped kofun |Length 75 meters |Construction of 3 stages. It has an early horizontal stone chamber similar to the ornamental Kofuns in the northwestern part of Kyushu. In the stone chamber, there is a stone partition carved with a straight arc pattern. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 6 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound |Diameter 30 meters |It has a horizontal stone chamber. |- |}

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
=== Details === ;Overall length: 350–360 meters ;Posterior circular portion: 190 meter diameter x 29 meter high, 3-tier ;Anterior rectangular portion: 215 meters wide x 25 meters high, 3-tier
<gallery> Tsukuriyamakofun02.jpg|Looking forward from the rear circular part Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), sekkan-1.jpg|Stone sarcophagus Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), sekkan-2.jpg|Fragments of stone sarcophagus </gallery>
=== ''Baizuka'' ===
{| class="wikitable" |- |Sakakiyama Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 1) |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} circuler mound or {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Rear circle diameter about 40m |A horse-shaped belt hook was excavated. In addition, a divine beast mirror and copper bells were excavated. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 2 |{{nihongo|''{{ill|Square Kofun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} square mound |About 40 meters on a side | Surrounding moat exists. More than 100 ''haniwa'' were unearthed in a row on the outer bank. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 3 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} (uncertain) |Diameter about 30 meters | |- |Tsukuriyama No. 4 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound or {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Length 55 meters |Cylindrical and figurative ''haniwa'' (house-shaped and armor-shaped) excavated from the edge of the mound. |- |Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5) |{{nihongo|{{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=''hotategata'' kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}|帆立貝形古墳||}} scallop-shaped kofun |Length 75 meters |Construction of 3 stages. It has an early horizontal stone chamber similar to the ornamental Kofuns in the northwestern part of Kyushu. In the stone chamber, there is a stone partition carved with a straight arc pattern. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 6 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound |Diameter 30 meters |It has a horizontal stone chamber. |- |}

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
=== Details === ;Overall length: 350–360 meters ;Posterior circular portion: 190 meter diameter x 29 meter high, 3-tier ;Anterior rectangular portion: 215 meters wide x 25 meters high, 3-tier
<gallery> Tsukuriyamakofun02.jpg|Looking forward from the rear circular part Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), sekkan-1.jpg|Stone sarcophagus Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), sekkan-2.jpg|Fragments of stone sarcophagus </gallery>
=== ''Baizuka'' ===
{| class="wikitable" |- |Sakakiyama Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 1) |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} circuler mound or {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Rear circle diameter about 40m |A horse-shaped belt hook was excavated. In addition, a divine beast mirror and copper bells were excavated. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 2 |{{nihongo|''{{ill|Square Kofun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} square mound |About 40 meters on a side | Surrounding moat exists. More than 100 ''haniwa'' were unearthed in a row on the outer bank. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 3 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} (uncertain) |Diameter about 30 meters | |- |Tsukuriyama No. 4 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound or {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Length 55 meters |Cylindrical and figurative ''haniwa'' (house-shaped and armor-shaped) excavated from the edge of the mound. |- |Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5) |{{nihongo|{{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=''hotategata'' kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}|帆立貝形古墳||}} scallop-shaped kofun |Length 75 meters |Construction of 3 stages. It has an early horizontal stone chamber similar to the ornamental Kofuns in the northwestern part of Kyushu. In the stone chamber, there is a stone partition carved with a straight arc pattern. |- |Tsukuriyama No. 6 |{{nihongo|''{{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} circular mound |Diameter 30 meters |It has a horizontal stone chamber. |- |}

The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
=== Details === ;Overall length: 350–360 meters ;Posterior circular portion: 190 meter diameter x 29 meter high, 3-tier ;Anterior rectangular portion: 215 meters wide x 25 meters high, 3-tier

{{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Tsukuriyama Kofun | native_name =造山古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Tsukuriyama Kofun, Okayama air.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_type = Japan Okayama Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Tsukuriyama Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E|region:JP-33|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], [[Japan]] | region = [[San'yō region]] | type = Kofun | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = early 5th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (museum) | other_designation = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|40|25.63|N|133|48|13.35|E}}}}}} [[file:Tsukuriyama Kofun (Okayama), zenkei.jpg|right|270px|thumb|Panoramic View]] {{nihongo|'''Tsukuriyama Kofun'''|造山古墳|}} is a cluster of [[Kofun period]] [[kofun|Kofun]]s located in the Shinjōshita neighborhood of [[Kita-ku, Okayama]], [[Okayama Prefecture]], in the [[San'yō region]] of [[Japan]]. The cluster was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1921.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/1916121|title=造山古墳 第一、二、三、四、五、六古墳 |language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2022}}</ref> The main Tsukuriyama Kofun is the largest Kofun in Okayama Prefecture and the fourth largest in Japan.
==Overview== The Tsukuriyama Kofun is a {{nihongo|''[[zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. The tumulus was built by cutting a hill on the right bank of the Ashimori River in the western part of Okayama city. The tumulus consists of three tiers, and each tier was lined with cylindrical ''[[haniwa]]'' and covered with ''[[fukiishi]]''. It has a length of approximately 350 meters, and is estimated to have been built in the first half of the 5th century. A characteristic of this Kofun is that the ratio of the posterior circular portion to the length of the mound is large. The anterior portion is thought to have been modified in the [[Sengoku period]], when a [[Shinto shrine]] was constructed, and a hamlet exists on the southeastern end of the mound. The ''[[chozubachi]]'' placed next the shrine is the body part of a hollowed-out [[sarcophagus]] made of [[tuff]], and fragments of the lid of the sarcophagus are scattered on the right side of the shrine. This sarcophagus is presumed to have been robbed from one of the tumuli in this area at some unknown date. From the size of the tumulus, it is believed to be the tomb of the 5th century kings of the [[Kingdom of Kibi]]. The posterior portion was also flattened and was used as a fortification and lookout point during [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]'s invasion of western Japan.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
Although it is the largest tumulus not under the control of the [[Imperial Household Agency]], full-scale academic research has not been conducted to date, and the interior has not yet been [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], so details of the [[burial chamber]] and [[grave goods]] are unknown. From 2009 to 2012, a research team from [[Okayama University]] conducted an excavation outside of the designated historic site for the purpose of identifying the scale at the time of construction, the existence of a surrounding moat, and for confirmation of relics that can be used to estimate the construction period. As a result, the existence of a surrounding 20-meter wide moat was confirmed on the east side of the posterior circular portion, and a large number of ''haniwa'' fragments from various shapes of ''haniwa'' was recovered. In 2016, a portion of the tumulus slope collapsed due to heavy rain.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
There are six smaller ''kofun'' in the surrounding area, which are regarded to being ''baizuka'', or ancillary tombs, for the main Tsukuriyama Kofun. The Senzoku Kofun (Tsukuriyama No. 5 Kofun) is a rare decorated ''kofun'', with paintings of magical symbols on the stone walls of the horizontal stone burial chamber. This keyhole-shaped tumulus has a total length of 75 meters. It was robbed in antiquity, and a stone sarcophagus remains in its anterior portion. In October 2009, the paintings were found to be detecting from the walls due to water damage, and the growth of mold was found to be problem in May 2010, leading to academic researchers detaching the murals for preservation.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The {{nihongo|Tsukuriyama Kofun Visitor Center|造山古墳ビジターセンター||}} was opened in April 2020.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
